clue.text: Local tenor looks silly in stiff attire

indicators.note: looking silly suggests the words local tenor are jumbled into a ridiculous new order

explanation.surface: A tenor in the local choir looks foolish in his formal starched clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks silly' rearranges the letters of LOCAL TENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: This broad starched white collar, worn by boys at a famous English public school, is rigid formal dress.

clue.text: Cheese manufactured the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word for manufactured is read from right to left

parts.note: manufactured means made

explanation.surface: A cheese that was produced badly at the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns MADE round to give the Dutch cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A round Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, named after its home town.

clue.text: Not participating, having no option but to drink gin neat?

definitions.text: having no option but to drink gin neat?

explanation.surface: Someone excluded from the party, forced to drink spirits undiluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is Italian vermouth, as in the old bar order gin and it; if you are out of It, your gin comes neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left out is excluded from the action; and lacking the vermouth called It means the mixer has run out.

clue.text: It's often covered by one going round in circles

definitions.text: It's often covered by one going round in circles

parts.words: It's often covered by one going round in circles
parts.note: someone circling a track travels the whole outer boundary line of the circle, lap after lap

explanation.surface: Something an aimless person keeps traversing as they get nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round in circles' sounds like futile effort, but literally a runner on a circular path covers its perimeter.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter distance around a circle is what someone travelling around it covers.

clue.text: Cosmetic nearly all spilt, knocked over on cover of mattress

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means the shortened word is turned upside down, reading bottom to top
nearly all of the word spilt is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tick, or ticking, is the strong fabric case of a mattress or pillow

explanation.surface: Makeup that was mostly spilled and toppled onto a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' cuts SPILT to SPIL, which 'knocked over' reverses to LIPS, placed above TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colour applied from a tube is a standard item of makeup.

clue.text: Space in which Roman's end would be seen?

definitions.text: Space in which Roman's end would be seen?

parts.words: Space in which Roman's end would be seen?
parts.note: an ancient Roman gladiator or condemned man would meet his death in front of crowds in the amphitheatre

explanation.surface: Asks where an ancient Roman might be seen to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman's end' looks like a letter-picking instruction, but it means a Roman's death, staged in the amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanded central floor of a Roman amphitheatre was where gladiators fought and died.

clue.text: Name of German unaffected by setback

indicators.note: a name not changed when set back reads the same in reverse as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A German man's name that survives a reverse unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unaffected by setback' says the name reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A common German masculine given name, borne by Bismarck among others.

clue.text: A number of busy workers who must deal with letters?

parts.note: ten is a number
ants are proverbially industrious workers

explanation.surface: Postal staff who handle the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' are not mail but people who let property, landlords, whom renters must deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Renters must deal with the landlords who lease property to them.

clue.text: Manias shown by old boys having meetings

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, and serves for the plural too
sessions are meetings, as of a committee

explanation.surface: Former schoolboys' reunions reveal their fixations.
explanation.definitionFit: Manias and fixations are both compulsive preoccupations of the mind.

clue.text: Gangster and sailor may be seen in church

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A mobster and a seaman turn up at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is Al Capone, the Prohibition-era gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table at the east end is the focal feature found in a church.

clue.text: Birds hard for country folk to bag

indicators.note: bagging something puts it inside, so the country folk enclose the letter for hard

parts.note: peasants are rural workers
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Game birds that rural people find difficult to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' suggests shooting game, but here it means enclose: H goes inside PEASANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-tailed game birds commonly shot in Britain.

clue.text: She may like getting her apple — or her chocolates possibly!

definitions.text: She may like getting her apple

indicators.note: possibly signals that the words her chocolates could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A woman enjoys receiving fruit or perhaps sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HER CHOCOLATES; pupils traditionally gave their teacher an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Children traditionally bring an apple as a gift for the woman who teaches their class.

clue.text: They show you healthy food so you can lose pounds!

definitions.text: They show you healthy food so you can lose pounds!

parts.words: They show you healthy food so you can lose pounds!
parts.note: gambling devices display cherries and lemons on their reels and swallow your money

explanation.surface: Sounds like diet aids that display nutritious fare to help you slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose pounds' suggests weight loss, but it is cash lost on a gaming machine in a British pub or arcade; the reels show symbols such as cherries.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin-operated gambling devices, also called one-armed bandits, have reels marked with symbols like cherries.

clue.text: Be irritated after unfortunate lapses in rep's presentation

indicators.note: after means the piece for be irritated comes behind the jumbled letters
unfortunate suggests the word lapses has gone wrong and is jumbled

parts.note: to itch is to be irritated

explanation.surface: Annoyance after some regrettable slips during a salesman's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' rearranges LAPSES to SALESP; 'after' places ITCH behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesperson's persuasive patter to a customer.

clue.text: Human object made with skill, one female exploit

parts.note: art means skill
I is the Roman numeral for one
an exploit is a deed or act

explanation.surface: A crafted item, and a woman's achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: An item made by people, especially of archaeological interest, as opposed to a natural one.

clue.text: Small tree in wild parts of Bosnia

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the word Bosnia run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A stunted tree growing in the rugged Balkan countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges BOSNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese art of growing dwarfed potted trees, and the miniature trees themselves.

clue.text: See mists swirling — it can make you most confused

indicators.note: swirling means the letters of see mists are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching fog swirl around can leave you disoriented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges SEE MISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of untidy or muddled: the most chaotic.

clue.text: Supreme control established by politician in republic

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for politician is placed inside the name of the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Absolute power set up by a politician in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: MP goes inside EIRE, the Irish name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial rule, sovereign authority over a wide domain, is total command.

clue.text: Plant seen around African city, short bedding plant

indicators.note: seen around means the plant word surrounds the shortened city

parts.note: a pea is a plant

indicators.note: short means the city name loses its last letter

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A plant spotted near a North African city, a little bedding plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the definition but supplies PEA; 'short' trims TUNIS to TUNI, which 'seen around' puts inside PEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly flowered annual widely used in summer flowerbeds.

clue.text: Writer with label on in military establishment

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A journalist with a name badge inside a defence headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end after the link 'in'; the US Department of Defense is housed in this five-sided building.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided US Department of Defense headquarters, a byword for the American military.

clue.text: Untidy garden on a Caribbean island

indicators.note: an untidy garden is one in disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A neglected garden on a West Indian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' rearranges GARDEN to GRENAD, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian island nation known as the Spice Isle.

clue.text: Outdone but likely to keep cool?

explanation.surface: Beaten, yet able to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for being overshadowed; read literally, something placed out of the sun keeps cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overshadowed by someone better is the idiom's sense; literally, placing something out of direct sunlight keeps its temperature down.

clue.text: Modest but losing head in a hurry

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for modest is removed

parts.note: chaste means modest or pure

explanation.surface: A demure person loses their composure in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the C off CHASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or rush in doing something.

clue.text: Meat bringing complaint

explanation.surface: Steak that prompts a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh of cattle eaten as food; and an informal word for a grievance.

clue.text: Playwright Williams is in a state

explanation.surface: An American dramatist lives in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The dramatist of A Streetcar Named Desire shares his first name with a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of A Streetcar Named Desire bore this first name, which is also a southern US state.

clue.text: Big effort but supreme happiness isn't quite achieved

indicators.note: isn't quite means the word for supreme happiness falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: heaven means supreme happiness or bliss

explanation.surface: A huge exertion, yet perfect bliss remains just out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't quite' drops the last letter of HEAVEN; 'achieved' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A strenuous pull or push, a great exertion of strength.

clue.text: Passion shown in early part of competition

explanation.surface: Intense emotion on display during a preliminary round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour or intensity of feeling; and a qualifying round of a race or contest.

clue.text: Wife getting a small beer preferable to the last one?

parts.note: better means preferable to what came before
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A man's new wife is an improvement over his previous one, over a modest drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'half' is half a pint, a small serving of beer in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular term for one's spouse, especially a wife.
